t.E479b.agn: In 2018 EFSA did not set a numerical ADI; by comparing a NOAEL of 5,400 mg/kg body weight from long-term rat studies with the highest estimated exposure of 10.1 mg/kg body weight in toddlers, it calculated a margin of safety of 540. Also taking into account that current use is limited, it found no safety concern; it noted that data on absorption/metabolism and developmental toxicity were insufficient.
t.E479b.body: There are no reliable data on how this substance is absorbed, processed and excreted in the body.
t.E479b.eval: It is obtained from soybean oil (relevant for people with soy allergy).
t.E479b.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by reacting thermally oxidised soybean oil with mono- and diglycerides under vacuum.
t.E479b.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no ADI set, no safety concern at the limited current use based on a margin-of-safety approach.
t.E479b.summary: An emulsifier produced from thermally oxidised soybean oil. It is used in frying fats to reduce spattering.
t.E479b.what: It is an emulsifier that reduces spattering in frying fat emulsions.
t.flag.allergen_soy_possible.0: It may be derived from soy. If you have a soy allergy, check whether the source is stated on the label.
